about: Every key of the 8 vendor Odia keyboards (C:/Shree-Lipi nxt/*.ORI, loaded from their original paths) answered by S8OriU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Ori764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes; the 4/5/6 fonts draw the same bytes, ₹ = 3C exists in WORI7001/2 only). Two capture runs (capvo/, capvo-b/) were identical (after normalising the random unit count the 7 composer returns for "no answer"), and each run asked every key twice (#stable 1); every load verified in SLNXT's shared table (#loaded 1). layer 0 = printed keyboard (normal and shift are different ASCII keys), layer 1 = Ctrl+Space, layer 2 = the composer raw code layer (key char = internal code; NOT the Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer, which the tutor does not expose - see ctrlShift1). Per key: codes = the internal codes the key holds (a conjunct slot expanded, typed order), uHex/u = the Unicode composer answer raw / without its carrier, b7 = the 7 composer bytes. u null = no answer or a placeholder ("Lk" = the link code 64 alone); b7 "07" = the 7 composer shows a lone sign on byte 07 in phonetic mode (no font has 07).

ctrlShift1.source: the vendor charts (CHM "Special Keys", the same 20 keys in all 9 Odia charts: assets/config/layouts/ori-*.json and odia-inscript.json "symbols") + the composers' answers for the internal code of each character (single-code probes, capp/P-results.json). b7 null = the 7 composer types nothing for that code.
